permit_text: FACILITY DESCRIPTION The City of Morro Bay currently discharges to the existing Morro Bay/Cayucos Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) under Order No. R3-2017-0050, NPDES No. CA0047881. The Central Coast Water Board issued Time Schedule Order No. R3- CITY OF MORRO BAY WATER RECLAMATION FACILITYORDER NO. R3-2022-0029 NPDES NO. CA3000002 ATTACHMENT F – FACT SHEET F-52018-0019 to the City of Morro Bay and the Cayucos Sanitary District requiring compliance with Order No. R3-2017-0050. Within the schedule necessitated by Time Schedule Order No. R3-2018-0019, the Discharger is constructing the City of Morro Bay Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) as part of the Morro Bay Our Water Program, which was designed to provide the City of Morro Bay with efficient, reliable, and adaptable wastewater treatment, while also producing a high-quality water supply to benefit the community. Wastewater from the City of Morro Bay will continue to be treated at and discharged from the existing Morro Bay/Cayucos WWTP under Order No. R3-2017-0050 until the constructed Facility and conveyance pipeline is fully operational. With the project fully operational, wastewater from the City of Morro Bay will be treated at and discharged from the new Facility to the existing ocean outfall. The new WRF will replace the existing WWTP with a membrane bioreactor (MBR) wastewater treatment facility that will produce tertiary treated effluent that exceeds secondary standards for discharge. The Facility also includes the Stormwater Adaptive Filtration Equipment (SAFE) system that will produce primary treated effluent during wet weather events, and an indirect potable reuse (IPR) advanced purification system that will produce advanced treated water for groundwater recharge and reverse osmosis (RO) concentrate that will be discharged to the ocean outfall. The Facility will have an average annual dry weather design flow of 0.97 million gallons per day (MGD). The Discharger plans to initiate Facility operations by July 2022 and expects the Facility to be fully operational by September 2022. 2.1. Description of Wastewater and Biosolids Treatment and Controls The Discharger owns and will operate the Facility, which will provide municipal and industrial wastewater services to a population of approximately 10,600 people in the City of Morro Bay. The Facility construction includes infrastructure, pipelines, and appurtenances for influent, effluent, and recycled water. 2.1.1. Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) System Raw wastewater will be conveyed to the Facility headworks, which will include two coarse screen and grit removal trains, a SAFE system box, and two parallel fine screens. Screenings and grit from the headworks facilities will be hauled offsite for disposal. Screened effluent and return activated sludge will flow into two biological nutrient removal (BNR) basins and then pumped to the MBR. The BNR-MBR basins will be configured as two parallel activated sludge treatment trains, each consisting of pre-anoxic, aerobic, and post-anoxic basins in-series. Filtrate from the MBR will be stored in two RO feed tanks, which will provide water for onsite uses and feed water to the RO system which produces water for IPR. Overflows from these tanks will be discharged to an outfall balancing tank. Tertiary treated effluent from the outfall balancing tank will be pumped through an outfall disinfection chlorine contact pipeline and will then be dechlorinated by sodium bisulfite injection prior to discharge through the ocean outfall. 2.1.2. Stormwater Adaptive Filtration Equipment (SAFE) System Wet weather flows exceeding the MBR treatment capacity of 1.88 MGD will flow by gravity through the SAFE box at the Facility headworks to the SAFE system. A CITY OF MORRO BAY WATER RECLAMATION FACILITYORDER NO. R3-2022-0029 NPDES NO. CA3000002 ATTACHMENT F – FACT SHEET F-6concrete tank, called the SAFE settling basin, will capture and equalize the wet weather flows prior to entering the SAFE filter system. Low wet weather flow volumes that do not completely fill the SAFE settling basin will be pumped back to the SAFE box for treatment when flows have decreased. The SAFE settling tank will have separate piping connected to the sludge dewatering pumps to provide the capability to operate one dewatering pump to drain the tank and the other to process sludge. During higher volume peak flow events, effluent will fill the SAFE settling basin, which will provide sedimentation treatment, until it passes over a weir and flows to the SAFE filter system for filtration treatment. Primary treated effluent from the SAFE filter system will then be routed to the outfall balancing tank where it will be blended with tertiary-treated MBR effluent and pumped by the outfall pump station to the outfall disinfection pipeline contactor and then the ocean outfall. Design flow of the SAFE settling basin and SAFE filter system is 6.26 MGD. 2.1.3. Indirect Potable Reuse (IPR) System Tertiary-treated effluent from the RO feed tanks may be sent to the outfall balancing tank or the IPR system for advanced purification. IPR system treatment consists of cartridge filters, an RO system, ultraviolet disinfection with advanced oxidation (UV/AOP) chlorination, and a calcite contactor. The IPR system was designed to accept a feed annual flow rate of 0.97 MGD and a peak hourly flow of 1.16 MGD. The RO recovery rate is expected to be between 80 and 85 percent, such that for average influent flow rates of 0.97 MGD, the RO permeate would be approximately 0.80 MGD, and the RO concentrate stream would be 0.17 MGD. Discharged RO concentrate will range between 0.05 and 0.23 MGD, depending on the influent flow rate. IPR product water that does not meet the requirements for recycling and RO concentrate will be diverted to the outfall balancing tank for discharge to the ocean outfall. RO concentrate will also be diverted directly to the RO concentrate disinfection contact pipeline for chlorination prior to commingling with the outfall disinfection contact pipeline upstream of the dechlorination injection point. 2.1.4. Ocean Outfall Transmission Main Effluent to be discharged to the Pacific Ocean at Discharge Point 001 will flow to an ocean outfall transmission main leading from the Facility to the ocean outfall pipeline. Additional waste streams that will discharge to the ocean outfall transmission main include saline waste from an industrial user and RO concentrate from the existing drinking water well system. Up to 0.0027 MGD of saline waste will be metered into the transmission main downstream of the WRF effluent or trucked to an off-site facility for treatment and disposal. In addition, up to 0.446 MGD of RO concentrate from the brackish water RO facility will be metered into the transmission main downstream of the WRF and industrial user or discharged through the current Vistra ocean outfall as a low threat discharge. 2.1.5. Biosolids The sludge holding tanks will receive, store, and aerate activated sludge wasted from the BNR MBR process. The holding tanks will consist of a two cell design, with each zone including mixers and bubble diffusers. It is expected that under normal operations only one zone will be in use to minimize sludge age for optimization of dewatering system performance. The sludge dewatering system will pump waste sludge from the sludge holding tanks, or directly from the MBR system, and dewatered by a belt filter press with a polymer storage and feed system. Dewatered biosolids will be transported offsite for beneficial use or landfill.
